Name: Act No. 90-559 of 4 July, 1990 establishing the foundations of enterprises and amending the provisions of Act No. 87-571 of 23 July, 1987 on the development of patronage relating to foundations
Objective: This law establishes the legal framework for the creation, operation, and regulation of corporate foundations in France, including their formation, governance, resources, and dissolution. It amends previous legislation to clarify the requirements for recognition, reporting, and oversight of foundations, particularly those created by companies for public interest purposes.

Provisions.Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE 1. [Government] [must] [create or appoint agency to implement and enforce the law] [at law’s commencement] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Provisions.Evidence: Art. 19-10. - The administrative authority shall ensure the regularity of the operation of the company Foundation; to this end, it can be given all documents and carry out any useful investigations. ... Art. 19-13. - A decree in Council of State lays down detailed rules for the application of articles 18 to 19-12 of this law.
Provisions.Explanation: The law assigns oversight and enforcement to an administrative authority and provides for further implementation by decree, fulfilling the requirement to appoint an agency.

Provisions.Provision: PERMISSIVE GOVERNANCE 1. [Agency] [must] [explain penalty for particular offenses, or explain a ‘general penalty’ for offenses where no penalty is expressly provided] [before commencement of the law] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Provisions.Evidence: Art. 20.- ... Presidents, directors or directors of groups who violate the provisions of this article shall be punished by a fine of 5000F to 15000F and, in the case of recidivism, by a fine of 10,000F to 30,000F.
Provisions.Explanation: Article 20 provides explicit penalties for violations, fulfilling the requirement for explanation of penalties.

Provisions.Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE 2. [CSOs] [must] [accept restricted freedoms on certain matters] [after law’s commencement] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]
Provisions.Evidence: Art. 19-8. ... Under penalty of withdrawal of the administrative authorization provided for in the article 19-1, the company Foundation cannot make call to the public generosity; it cannot receive donations nor bequests.
Provisions.Explanation: The law restricts company foundations from public fundraising and receiving donations/bequests, with penalties for non-compliance.

Provisions.Explanation: The law allows for regulatory details to be set by decree, which is an alternative to the normal legislative process.

Provisions.Explanation: The National Council provides oversight and accountability for the regulation of foundations.

Provisions.Explanation: Legal capacity is only granted upon administrative authorization and publication, requiring formal registration.

If the Board has not been able to proceed with this nomination or if the dissolution results from the withdrawal of authorization, the liquidator is designated the judicial authority. The appointment of the liquidator is published in the Official Gazette.
Provisions.Explanation: The law provides explicit procedures for dissolution and liquidation.
